extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of 19th-century literature and social-philosophical essays (Carlyle)
extracted.subtask_description: Close reading / extraction of evaluative aphorisms and social-philosophical prescriptions from an excerpt of Thomas Carlyle's Sartor Resartus (Teufelsdrockh sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: True education vs appearance of education
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nameless University is condemned for producing appearance rather than real instruction: 'These Professors in the Nameless lived with ease, with safety, by a mere Reputation... They themselves needed not to work; their attempts at working, at what they called Educating, now when I look back on it, fill me with a certain mute admiration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance is embedded as critique and examples: universities may have impressive mechanical structures and declared claims (admission-fees, professorial titles) yet yield no real teaching; beware institutions that trade on reputation instead of producing learning. Anti-pattern: mistaking 'reputation' or 'declaration aloud' for genuine educational outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistics of imposture (ware vs appearance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed evaluative metric: measure how much social output is real 'Ware' versus mere 'Appearance of Ware' — Carlyle suggests the ratio of real to apparent product may be as low as One to a Hundred in Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrounding exposition calls for an inquiry into how much of government's, religion's, education's output is genuine performance vs. puffery (Puffery, Quackery, Priestcraft, Kingcraft). Examples: Professors grinding on reputation, the economic value produced by 'puffery' vs actual service. Use as a skeptical diagnostic for institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gullibility/imposture as temporary social anodyne
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposture and the public's gullibility can sometimes play a sanative or anodyne role in desperate circumstances: '...probably Imposture is of sanative, anodyne nature, and man's Gullibility not his worst blessing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by the analogy of an insolvent army being fed with 'fairy-money' to prevent mutiny until real supplies arrive. Guidance: recognize that appearances/impostures can temporarily stabilize social systems; anti-pattern is romanticizing imposture as permanent good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professions/apprenticeships as practical devices (pros and cons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Professions and indentures channel vague youthful capacities into a specific craftsman-role: 'Indentures and Apprenticeships... whereby, in due season, the vague universality of a Man shall find himself ready-moulded into a specific Craftsman.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pros: reduce waste of time, provide livelihood ('Bread-studies'), give the blind-born spiritual artist practical purpose. Cons: can act as a 'neck-halter' that throttles original talent; may prevent fuller realization if misapplied. Use as a pragmatic trade-off when advising vocational direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thinking/Thought as thaumaturgic power
rubrics_metrics.description: Thought is described as thaumaturgic — a primary engine of social and material miracles: 'Thaumaturgic I name it; for hitherto all Miracles have been wrought thereby... Has he not seen the Scottish Brass-smith's IDEA... travelling on fire-wings round the Cape...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: value and cultivate thinking because it produces transformative inventions and social change (steam-engines example). Anti-pattern: undervaluing intellectual work as idle or purely speculative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardest problem: identify combined inward and outward capability
rubrics_metrics.description: The first and hardest problem for a young person is to discover 'what your combined inward and outward Capability specially is' — matching inner talent to external circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many years are wasted 'groping' and clutching wrong pursuits; practical implication: deliberate self-study and assessment of environment are required to find the vocation that best fits talents and fortunes. Anti-pattern: drifting from enterprise to enterprise without convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sarcasm/irony as defensive technique but socially corrosive
rubrics_metrics.description: Sarcasm functions as defensive armor ('the panoply of Sarcasm was but as a buckram case') yet is harmful: 'Sarcasm I now see to be, in general, the language of the Devil.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance cautions that while irony may protect a sensitive person, it provokes hostility and isolates one socially; anti-pattern: habitual ironic tone used to shield oneself, which leads to being disliked and undermines constructive relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hunger/necessity as driver to practical choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Hunger (necessity) forces prompt vocational choice and can prevent wasteful indecision: 'For on this ground, as the prompt nature of Hunger is well known, must a prompt choice be made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: economic pressure can push youth into apprenticeship or trades that secure livelihood and sharpen capabilities. Warning: if the enforced choice is inappropriate, it can become a 'neck-halter' limiting higher talents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationalist education risks scepticism or self-conceit
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Rational University,' hostile to mysticism, tends to produce two results: the better sort end in 'sick, impotent Scepticism,' the worse explode into 'finished Self-conceit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a critique of one-sided rationalist pedagogy: balance is needed to avoid producing dry sceptics or arrogant know-it-alls. Anti-pattern: teaching progress-of-species rhetoric that inflates argumentativeness without cultivating depth of belief or moral purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and continuous work as moral duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Human existence is time-bound and thus requires continual movement and right-directed work: 'Our Whole Duty, which is to move, to work,--in the right direction. Are not our Bodies and our Souls in continual movement... Time devours all his Children.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance frames industrious activity as moral imperative and existential necessity; anti-pattern: passivity or 'excellent Passivity' that prevents engagement and leads to inner stagnation.
